title: Customers in a city
prompt: Show each city and its customer names in alphabetical order, joined with commas, as residents.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT city, GROUP_CONCAT(name ORDER BY name) AS residents FROM customers GROUP BY city;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT city, GROUP_CONCAT(name ORDER BY name DESC) AS residents FROM customers GROUP BY city;
SELECT city, COUNT(*) AS residents FROM customers GROUP BY city;

title: Name format
prompt: Show the full_name of contacts whose name is two words, each starting with a capital letter.
hints: A pattern with exactly one space.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM contacts; INSERT INTO contacts VALUES (11, 'mary jackson', 'mary-j@club.test', '555-0111', 'Hampton', 'SILVER GOLD1'), (12, 'BOB Kahn', 'bob@CLUB.test', '555-0112', NULL, 'gold1'), (13, 'Rosa Park', 'rosa@club-test', NULL, 'Tuskegee', 'NEW'), (14, 'Ken Thompson', 'ken.t@club.test', '5550114', 'Murray', 'GOLD3'); UPDATE contacts SET full_name = 'Ken' WHERE id = 14;

solutions: SELECT full_name FROM contacts WHERE full_name REGEXP '^[A-Z][a-zA-Z]* [A-Z][a-zA-Z]*$';

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT full_name FROM contacts WHERE full_name LIKE '% %';
SELECT full_name FROM contacts WHERE full_name REGEXP '^[A-Z]';

title: Devices by date
prompt: Show each device and its different session dates in order, joined with a comma and space, as dates.
hints: DISTINCT uses the default comma, so build it with a subquery.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM sessions; DELETE FROM users; INSERT INTO users VALUES (7, 'sable', NULL, '2024-02-27'), (8, 'tulip', 7, '2024-02-28'), (9, 'umber', 7, '2024-03-01'); INSERT INTO sessions VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 50, 'web'), (12, 7, '2024-02-29', 50, 'web'), (13, 7, '2024-03-01', 7, 'ios'), (14, 8, '2024-03-02', 33, 'android'); INSERT INTO sessions VALUES (15, 7, '2024-02-28', 5, 'web');

solutions: SELECT device, GROUP_CONCAT(session_date, ', ' ORDER BY session_date) AS dates FROM (SELECT DISTINCT device, session_date FROM sessions) GROUP BY device;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT device, GROUP_CONCAT(session_date, ', ' ORDER BY session_date) AS dates FROM sessions GROUP BY device;
SELECT device, GROUP_CONCAT(session_date, ',' ORDER BY session_date) AS dates FROM (SELECT DISTINCT device, session_date FROM sessions) GROUP BY device;

title: City tags
prompt: Show each known city and how many contacts have a tag starting with GOLD, in exact capitals, as gold, including 0.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM contacts; INSERT INTO contacts VALUES (11, 'mary jackson', 'mary-j@club.test', '555-0111', 'Hampton', 'SILVER GOLD1'), (12, 'BOB Kahn', 'bob@CLUB.test', '555-0112', NULL, 'gold1'), (13, 'Rosa Park', 'rosa@club-test', NULL, 'Tuskegee', 'NEW'), (14, 'Ken Thompson', 'ken.t@club.test', '5550114', 'Murray', 'GOLD3');

solutions: SELECT city, SUM(CASE WHEN tags GLOB 'GOLD*' OR tags GLOB '* GOLD*' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS gold FROM contacts WHERE city IS NOT NULL GROUP BY city;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT city, COUNT(*) AS gold FROM contacts WHERE tags GLOB 'GOLD*' GROUP BY city;
SELECT city, SUM(CASE WHEN tags LIKE '%GOLD%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS gold FROM contacts WHERE city IS NOT NULL GROUP BY city;

title: Grades per student
prompt: Show each student's name and their known grades from highest to lowest, separated by a slash, as grades.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring');

solutions: SELECT s.name, GROUP_CONCAT(e.grade, '/' ORDER BY e.grade DESC) AS grades FROM students s JOIN enrolments e ON e.student_id = s.id GROUP BY s.id, s.name;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT s.name, GROUP_CONCAT(e.grade, '/' ORDER BY e.grade) AS grades FROM students s JOIN enrolments e ON e.student_id = s.id GROUP BY s.id, s.name;
SELECT s.name, GROUP_CONCAT(e.grade ORDER BY e.grade DESC) AS grades FROM students s JOIN enrolments e ON e.student_id = s.id GROUP BY s.id, s.name;
